Common gotchas to encode in the sketch + guide:

SD card FAT32 (not exFAT; ≤32GB cards are usually fine)
File naming: root folder, named 0001.mp3 (use play(1) which plays by index — actually myDFPlayer.play(1) plays the FIRST file by index; playMp3Folder(1) plays /mp3/0001.mp3). File naming matters less with play(n) since it's index-based, but sequential copy order can matter. Safest: name files 0001.mp3 etc.
1k resistor between ESP32 TX and DFPlayer RX when powering DFPlayer at 5V (its RX is 3.3V logic) — prevents damage and bus errors
Volume: don't set 30 (max) — clones distort/freeze above ~25
Some clones need 100ms+ between commands
"Unable to begin" errors → check wiring TX/RX crossing, SD card seating
If no sound but module responds: check speaker is on SPK_1/SPK_2, check file exists, volume
USB power: DFPlayer speaker can draw a lot; if ESP32 browns out (reboots when sound plays), power separately or lower volume
Busy pin (optional): LOW while playing — can be monitored
Keep speaker wires away from electrode wires (EMG noise) — from project docs

ESP32 tone: use ledc. On Arduino-ESP32 core 3.x, ledcAttach(pin, freq, res) / ledcWriteTone(pin, freq); on 2.x, ledcSetup/ledcAttachPin/ledcWriteTone. Version differences are a footgun. Simplest cross-version approach: square wave by bit-banging digitalWrite? Ugly. Or DAC sine? For a quick beep, bit-bang with delayMicroseconds is version-proof:

cpp


const int AUDIO_PIN = 25;
void beep(int ms) {
  for (long t = 0; t < ms * 1000L; t += 500) { // 1 kHz square
    digitalWrite(AUDIO_PIN, HIGH); delayMicroseconds(250);
    digitalWrite(AUDIO_PIN, LOW);  delayMicroseconds(250);
  }
}
1kHz square into PAM8403 → audible beep. Fine for plan B. Keep in guide only, not a separate file. Hmm, or make it a third file SpeakerTest_Amp_Tone.ino? One more check — the DFPlayer RX 1k resistor: when DFPlayer VCC=5V, its RX pin internal reference is 3.3V; direct 3.3V ESP32 TX is actually FINE (ESP32 GPIO26 outputs 3.3V — that's exactly what DFPlayer RX wants). The 1k is protective series resistance recommended because... actually the common advice: DFPlayer RX is 3.3V logic; ESP32 TX at 3.3V is safe WITHOUT resistor. The 1k recommendation is for 5V Arduinos. But many clone docs say add 1k anyway to limit current through the internal resistor (clone boards have 1k onboard already marked). Honest guidance: ESP32 3.3V TX → DFPlayer RX is safe directly; if comms are flaky, add a 1k. The project docs said "via 1k if needed" — consistent. Good.

Power: DFPlayer VCC → 5V (VIN on ESP32 dev board when USB powered). Speaker up to 3W can brown-out USB power — advise volume ≤ 24 and if ESP32 reboots on play, use volume lower / separate 5V supply with common GND.

File 1: SpeakerTest_DFPlayer.ino — careful, complete, well-commented, matching their v-series style.

cpp


/*
 * VocalBridge — SPEAKER TEST (DFPlayer Mini + speaker)
 * -----------------------------------------------------
 * Answers: "does my speaker work?"
 *
 * What it does:
 *   1) Boots, finds the DFPlayer and the SD card, prints a report
 *   2) Plays track 1 (0001.mp3 = "Help") ~2 s after boot
 *   3) Then obeys Serial Monitor commands (115200 baud):
 *
 *      1-9  play that track        + / -   volume up/down
 *      n    next track             b       previous track
 *      s    stop                   p       pause        r   resume
 *      l    loop track 1           h       reprint help
 *
 * Board:   ESP32 Dev Module
 * Wiring:  DFPlayer VCC -> VIN (5V)
 *          DFPlayer GND -> GND
 *          DFPlayer RX  -> GPIO26 (1k resistor in series if you have one)
 *          DFPlayer TX  -> GPIO27
 *          Speaker      -> SPK_1 and SPK_2  (NOT to GND!)
 *          microSD      -> FAT32, files in root: 0001.mp3, 0002.mp3, ...
 * Library: "DFRobotDFPlayerMini" (Library Manager)
 * Baud:    115200
 */
then code. Let me write it fully with care.

cpp


#include <DFRobotDFPlayerMini.h>
const int BAUD = 115200;
// Serial2 pins: RX=27 (ESP32 listens here <- DFPlayer TX)
//               TX=26 (ESP32 talks here   -> DFPlayer RX)
#define DF_RX_PIN 27
#define DF_TX_PIN 26
DFRobotDFPlayerMini player;
bool speakerOnline = false;
int volume = 20;                 // 0..30 — clones distort near 30, keep <= 25
unsigned long lastCmdMs = 0;
void setup() {
  Serial.begin(BAUD);
  delay(800);
  Serial.println();
  Serial.println("VocalBridge SpeakerTest — DFPlayer Mini");
  Serial.println("----------------------------------------");
  Serial2.begin(9600, SERIAL_8N1, DF_RX_PIN, DF_TX_PIN);
  // ---- find the DFPlayer (try 5 times) ----
  for (int i = 1; i <= 5 && !speakerOnline; i++) {
    Serial.print("Trying to find DFPlayer (attempt ");
    Serial.print(i); Serial.println("/5)...");
    speakerOnline = player.begin(Serial2, /*isACK*/ true, /*doReset*/ true);
    if (!speakerOnline) delay(400);
  }
  if (!speakerOnline) {
    Serial.println();
    Serial.println("!! DFPlayer NOT FOUND — sound test cannot run.");
    Serial.println("!! Check in this order:");
    Serial.println("!!   1. DFPlayer VCC -> 5V (VIN), GND -> GND");
    Serial.println("!!   2. DFPlayer RX -> GPIO26, DFPlayer TX -> GPIO27 (crossed!)");
    Serial.println("!!   3. microSD pushed fully in, FAT32, at least one .mp3");
    Serial.println("!!   4. Power the ESP32 from USB, not a weak battery");
    Serial.println();
    Serial.println("Staying alive so you can read this. Fix + press RST / re-upload.");
  } else {
    Serial.println(">> DFPlayer ONLINE.");
    delay(200);
    player.volume(volume);        // set a sane volume
    delay(100);
    int files = player.readFileCounts();
    Serial.print(">> SD card files found: ");
    Serial.println(files < 0 ? "unknown (card error?)" : String(files));
    Serial.println(">> Playing track 1 in 2 s — you should hear it NOW-ish.");
    Serial.println();
    printHelp();
    delay(2000);
    player.play(1);
  }
}

loop:

cpp


void loop() {
  if (!speakerOnline) { delay(5000); Serial.println("(still no DFPlayer — check wiring, then press RST)"); return; }
  // listen for DFPlayer events (errors, card changes)
  if (player.available()) printDetail(player.readType(), player.read());
  // serial commands
  if (Serial.available()) handleChar(Serial.read());
}
handleChar with debounce:

cpp


void handleChar(char c) {
  if (c == '\r' || c == '\n' || c == ' ') return;
  if (millis() - lastCmdMs < 150) return;   // clones glitch if commands are spammed
  lastCmdMs = millis();
  if (c >= '1' && c <= '9') { int t = c - '0'; Serial.print(">> play track "); Serial.println(t); player.play(t); }
  else if (c == '+') { volume += 2; clampVol(); player.volume(volume); volMsg(); }
  else if (c == '-') { volume -= 2; clampVol(); player.volume(volume); volMsg(); }
  else if (c == 'n') { Serial.println(">> next"); player.next(); }
  else if (c == 'b') { Serial.println(">> previous"); player.previous(); }
  else if (c == 's') { Serial.println(">> stop"); player.stop(); }
  else if (c == 'p') { Serial.println(">> pause"); player.pause(); }
  else if (c == 'r') { Serial.println(">> resume"); player.start(); }
  else if (c == 'l') { Serial.println(">> loop track 1 (send s to stop)"); player.loop(1); }
  else if (c == 'h' || c == '?') printHelp();
  else { Serial.print("?? unknown '"); Serial.write(c); Serial.println("' — send h for help"); }
}
Note: player.start() resumes. yes.

File 3: SpeakerTest_Tone_Amp.ino (plan B). Small:

cpp


/*
 * VocalBridge — SPEAKER TEST B (plain amp board, e.g. PAM8403)
 * Use this if your "driver" has NO microSD slot (it's just an amplifier).
 * ...
 * Wiring: amp VCC -> 5V(VIN), amp GND -> GND,
 *         amp input L(+) -> GPIO25 through 1k (if available),
 *         amp input GND(-) -> ESP32 GND, speaker -> amp OUT L + and -
 * Beep-beep-beep forever, 1 s apart. Loud enough = works.
 */
const int AUDIO_PIN = 25;
void setup() { pinMode(AUDIO_PIN, OUTPUT); Serial.begin(115200); }
void beep(int ms) {
  // 1 kHz square wave — no ledc/tone needed, works on any core version
  for (long t = 0; t < ms * 1000L; t += 500) {
    digitalWrite(AUDIO_PIN, HIGH); delayMicroseconds(250);
    digitalWrite(AUDIO_PIN, LOW);  delayMicroseconds(250);
  }
}
void loop() {
  Serial.println("beep x3 (1 kHz)");
  beep(150); delay(100); beep(150); delay(100); beep(300);
  delay(1000);
}

Core 2.x (driver/i2s.h):

cpp


#include <driver/i2s.h>
i2s_config_t i2s_config = {
  .mode = (i2s_mode_t)(I2S_MODE_MASTER | I2S_MODE_TX),
  .sample_rate = 16000,
  .bits_per_sample = I2S_BITS_PER_SAMPLE_16BIT,
  .channel_format = I2S_CHANNEL_FMT_ONLY_LEFT,  // MAX98357A mono: left channel
  .communication_format = I2S_COMM_FORMAT_STAND_I2S,
  .intr_alloc_flags = ESP_INTR_FLAG_LEVEL1,
  .dma_buf_count = 8,
  .dma_buf_len = 64,
  .use_apll = false,
  .tx_desc_auto_clear = true
};
i2s_pin_config_t pins = {
  .bck_io_num = 26, .ws_io_num = 25, .data_out_num = 22, .data_in_num = I2S_PIN_NO_CHANGE
};
i2s_driver_install(I2S_NUM_0, &i2s_config, 0, NULL);
i2s_set_pin(I2S_NUM_0, &pins);
i2s_write(I2S_NUM_0, buffer, bytes, &written, portMAX_DELAY);
Note: in core 2.x, .mck_io_num must be first member in newer versions — the mck field exists in IDF 4.4 (core 2.0.x). In Arduino .ino (C++), i2s_pin_config_t pins = { .mck_io_num = I2S_PIN_NO_CHANGE, .bck_io_num = 26, ... } — must include mck first for IDF4.4. For older core 1.0.6 (IDF 3.x) there's no mck. Most users are on core 2.x now. I'll write with mck_io_num included and add a comment. Actually, designated initializers in C++11 aren't standard (C99 feature) — GCC allows as extension, must be in declaration order. Fine.

On 2.x, ONLY_LEFT with 16-bit → each sample sent on left slot only; MAX98357A averages L+R → half amplitude, fine for a beep (compensate with volume scale up to 32767×? cap). OK.

Beep generation:

cpp


const int16_t sine16[16] = {0,12539,23170,30273,32767,30273,23170,12539,0,-12539,-23170,-30273,-32767,-30273,-23170,-12539};
void playTone(int ms, int freqHz) {
  // phase accumulator so any freq works
  uint32_t step = (uint32_t)(freqHz * 65536.0 / SAMPLE_RATE); // hmm use float
  uint32_t phase = 0;
  int total = SAMPLE_RATE * ms / 1000;
  int16_t buf[64];
  while (total > 0) {
    int n = min(64, total);
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
      buf[i] = (int16_t)((int32_t)sine16[(phase >> 12) & 0xF] * volumeScale / 21);
      phase += step;
    }
    writeI2S(buf, n*2);
    total -= n;
  }
}
volume scale: volume 0..21 → gain = volume/21.0 → multiply 32767-range sample by gain → int. Fine with int32 math: (sample * volume) / 21.*

writeI2S: core3: i2s.write((uint8_t*)buf, len) returns bytes; core2: i2s_write(I2S_NUM_0, buf, len, &written, portMAX_DELAY).*

Also 1kHz might be tinny on a 2″ woofer; use 440 Hz + 880 Hz — more audible/pleasant. Pattern: 880 short, 880 short, 440 long.

The sketch does NOT need the .wav files — the audio is already baked into help_sound.h (the C header with raw PCM data). The ESP32 cannot read .wav files directly from the repo — it only uses the header.

Future DFPlayer path: if you ever buy a DFPlayer Mini, you'd convert help_clean.wav to MP3, name it 0001.mp3, put on SD card
Archive/reference: keep the master copy so the voice can always be reproduced even if help_sound.h gets changed

Recommendation ladder:

Better: solder — they have the iron, it's the most reliable; speaker cone is delicate: solder quickly on the TAB, don't let the iron touch the cone, don't hold heat long (solder tab conducts heat into the voice coil — 2-3 seconds max)

Twisting can work for a quick test — electricity doesn't care how the wires meet — but let me give you the honest trade-off, because it's very relevant to the "sound comes sometime, then stops" problem you have right now.

The catch with twist-on speaker wires
A speaker line is different from your signal wires: it's a 4Ω connection, which means the amp pushes up to ~1 amp through it at full volume. Any spot where the twist is slightly loose acts like a flaky switch:

Intermittent contact → crackle, cutouts, sound that comes and goes ← exactly the symptom you described
The speaker itself vibrates while playing, physically shaking the joint loose mid-sound
The joint also gets moved every time you reposition the breadboard
Your project history is literally a witness to this: the entire 4095 saga was caused by one unsoldered, loose wire on the AD8232. Loose connections are this project's nemesis. 😄

Method	Reliability	Good for
Twist + electrical tape (twist tight, loop through the hole first, then tape)	⚠️ Works for today's chime test, degrades fast	Quick test only
Alligator/crocodile clips (if you have them)	⚠️ Same — okay for testing, rattles	Quick test only
Soldered	✅ Rock solid	The demo video, everything permanent

You soldered the AD8232 headers yourself — and that was the fiddly job (tiny pads, delicate chip). Speaker wires are easier: big tabs, big holes, nothing fragile nearby. So if that iron is still around, this is a 2-minute job:

How (safe speaker soldering):

Loop the bare wire through the hole/tab first — the mechanical loop carries the strain, the solder just locks it
Touch the iron to the tab, not the wire, ~2–3 seconds max
Feed a little solder, remove iron, hold still 5 s
⚠️ Never let the iron touch the speaker cone (the paper/metal diaphragm) and don't heat the tab for long — heat travels down the tab into the voice coil
Same on the MAX98357A's + and − holes: poke wire through, bend, solder
Two safety notes:

Make sure + and − never touch each other (a shorted speaker output, even briefly, isn't great for the amp)
Which wire goes to + vs − doesn't matter for one speaker — worst case the sound is "inverted," which your ear can't tell with a single speaker

Runtime table init:

c


#include <math.h>
int16_t SINE256[256];
void buildSine() {
  for (int i = 0; i < 256; i++)
    SINE256[i] = (int16_t)(32767.0 * sinf(2.0 * M_PI * i / 256.0));
}
M_PI availability: Arduino defines M_PI (in math.h with USE_MATH_DEFINES? on ESP32 core it's available — yes, ESP32 math.h provides M_PI). Safe: use 6.28318530718 literal to be bulletproof.

call buildSine() in setup() before first play. playTone:

c


void playTone(int freqHz, int ms) {
  uint32_t step  = (uint32_t)(((double)freqHz * 4294967296.0) / SAMPLE_RATE);
  uint32_t phase = 0;
  long total = (long)SAMPLE_RATE * ms / 1000;
  long fade  = SAMPLE_RATE / 50;
  if (fade * 2 > total) fade = total / 2;
  int16_t buf[64];
  long sent = 0;
  while (sent < total) {
    int n = 64;
    if (sent + n > total) n = (int)(total - sent);
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
      long idx = sent + i;
      int env = volume;
      if (idx < fade)               env = volume * idx / fade;
      else if (idx >= total - fade) env = volume * (total - idx) / fade;
      int32_t s = ((int32_t)SINE256[phase >> 24] * env) / 21;
      buf[i] = (int16_t)s;
      phase += step;
    }
    i2sWriteSamples(buf, n);
    sent += n;
  }
}

// play a pure tone for `ms` milliseconds at `freqHz` (with click-free fades)
void playTone(int freqHz, int ms) {
  uint32_t step  = (uint32_t)(((double)freqHz * 65536.0) / SAMPLE_RATE);
  uint32_t phase = 0;
  long total     = (long)SAMPLE_RATE * ms / 1000;     // total samples to send
  long fade      = SAMPLE_RATE / 50;                  // 20 ms fade in/out (no clicks)
  if (fade * 2 > total) fade = total / 2;
  int16_t buf[64];
  long sent = 0;
  while (sent < total) {
    int n = 64;
    if (sent + n > total) n = (int)(total - sent);
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
      long idx = sent + i;
      int env = volume;                               // flat middle part
      if (idx < fade)          env = (int)(volume * idx / fade);          // fade in

      buf[i] = (int16_t)s;
      phase += step;
    }
    i2sWriteSamples(buf, n);
    sent += n;
  }
}

1️⃣ SpeakerTest_MAX98357A.ino — the beep test (clean 256-step tone)
In Arduino IDE: File → New, delete everything, paste this, save as SpeakerTest_MAX98357A:

C++

/*
 * VocalBridge — SPEAKER TEST (MAX98357A I2S amp + speaker)
 * -------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Beep-beep-beeeep every 3 s = wiring is correct.
 * No library needed. Works on esp32 core v2.x AND v3.x.
 *
 * WIRING:  VIN->VIN(5V)  GND->GND  BCLK->GPIO27  LRC->GPIO26  DIN->GPIO25
 *          SD & GAIN unconnected, speaker -> + / -
 *          (if you moved LRC to GPIO33 during debugging, change PIN_LRC below)
 *
 * SERIAL (115200):  b = beep now, + / - = volume, h = help
 */

const int PIN_BCLK = 27;          // bit clock
const int PIN_LRC  = 26;          // left/right clock (word select)  <- set 33 if you moved it
const int PIN_DIN  = 25;          // data into the amp

const int BAUD       = 115200;
const int SAMPLE_RATE = 16000;

int volume = 10;                  // 0..21 — safe for a small speaker

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------
// I2S setup — auto-detects esp32 core v2 vs v3
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#if defined(ESP_ARDUINO_VERSION_MAJOR) && (ESP_ARDUINO_VERSION_MAJOR >= 3)
  // ---------- esp32 core 3.x ----------
  #include <ESP_I2S.h>
  I2SClass i2s;

  void i2sInit() {
    i2s.setPins(PIN_BCLK, PIN_LRC, PIN_DIN);
    i2s.begin(I2S_MODE_STD, SAMPLE_RATE, I2S_DATA_BIT_WIDTH_16BIT, I2S_SLOT_MODE_MONO);
  }
  void i2sWriteSamples(int16_t *buf, int count) {
    i2s.write((uint8_t *)buf, count * sizeof(int16_t));
  }
#else
  // ---------- esp32 core 2.x ----------
  #include <driver/i2s.h>

  void i2sInit() {
    i2s_config_t cfg = {
      .mode = (i2s_mode_t)(I2S_MODE_MASTER | I2S_MODE_TX),
      .sample_rate = SAMPLE_RATE,
      .bits_per_sample = I2S_BITS_PER_SAMPLE_16BIT,
      .channel_format = I2S_CHANNEL_FMT_ONLY_LEFT,     // mono; MAX98357A averages L+R
      .communication_format = I2S_COMM_FORMAT_STAND_I2S,
      .intr_alloc_flags = 0,
      .dma_buf_count = 8,
      .dma_buf_len = 64,
      .use_apll = false,
      .tx_desc_auto_clear = true
    };
    i2s_pin_config_t pins = {
      .mck_io_num = I2S_PIN_NO_CHANGE,
      .bck_io_num = PIN_BCLK,
      .ws_io_num = PIN_LRC,
      .data_out_num = PIN_DIN,
      .data_in_num = I2S_PIN_NO_CHANGE
    };
    i2s_driver_install(I2S_NUM_0, &cfg, 0, NULL);
    i2s_set_pin(I2S_NUM_0, &pins);
  }
  void i2sWriteSamples(int16_t *buf, int count) {
    size_t written = 0;
    i2s_write(I2S_NUM_0, buf, count * sizeof(int16_t), &written, portMAX_DELAY);
  }
#endif

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------
// Clean 256-step sine wave
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------
int16_t SINE256[256];

void buildSine() {
  for (int i = 0; i < 256; i++)
    SINE256[i] = (int16_t)(32767.0 * sinf(6.28318530718 * i / 256.0));
}

void playTone(int freqHz, int ms) {
  uint32_t step  = (uint32_t)(((double)freqHz * 4294967296.0) / SAMPLE_RATE);
  uint32_t phase = 0;
  long total     = (long)SAMPLE_RATE * ms / 1000;
  long fade      = SAMPLE_RATE / 50;
  if (fade * 2 > total) fade = total / 2;

  int16_t buf[64];
  long sent = 0;
  while (sent < total) {
    int n = 64;
    if (sent + n > total) n = (int)(total - sent);
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
      long idx = sent + i;
      int env = volume;
      if (idx < fade)                  env = volume * idx / fade;
      else if (idx >= total - fade)    env = volume * (total - idx) / fade;
      int32_t s = ((int32_t)SINE256[phase >> 24] * env) / 21;
      buf[i] = (int16_t)s;
      phase += step;
    }
    i2sWriteSamples(buf, n);
    sent += n;
  }
}

void playChime() {
  playTone(880, 150);  delay(120);
  playTone(880, 150);  delay(120);
  playTone(440, 450);
}

void volumeMsg() {
  Serial.print(">> volume = "); Serial.print(volume); Serial.println(" / 21");
}

void handleChar(char c) {
  if (c == '\r' || c == '\n' || c == ' ') return;
  if (c == 'b' || c == 'B') { Serial.println(">> beep!"); playChime(); }
  else if (c == '+') { if (volume < 21) volume++; volumeMsg(); }
  else if (c == '-') { if (volume > 0)  volume--; volumeMsg(); }
  else { Serial.print("?? '"); Serial.write(c); Serial.println("'"); }
}

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(BAUD);
  delay(800);
  Serial.println();
  Serial.println("VocalBridge SpeakerTest — MAX98357A (I2S) + speaker");
  Serial.println("----------------------------------------------------");
  i2sInit();
  buildSine();
  Serial.println(">> Chime in 2 seconds — LISTEN for beep-beep-beeeep.");
  volumeMsg();
  delay(2000);
}

void loop() {
  playChime();
  Serial.println("chime! (b = beep now, + / - = volume)");
  for (int t = 0; t < 300; t++) {
    if (Serial.available()) handleChar(Serial.read());
    delay(10);
  }
}
2️⃣ SpeakerSayHelp_MAX98357A.ino — says "Help!"
This one needs help_sound.h in the same folder (step 3 below). Save the sketch as SpeakerSayHelp_MAX98357A, paste:

C++

/*
 * VocalBridge — SPEAKER SAYS "HELP!" (MAX98357A, voice on-chip)
 * --------------------------------------------------------------------
 * The "Help!" voice is INSIDE the ESP32 (help_sound.h) — no SD card.
 * Says "Help!" 2 s after boot. Then (Serial @115200):
 *   h = say it   2 = twice   l = loop every 3 s   + / - = volume
 *   b = beep chime   i = info
 *
 * WIRING: same as beep test — VIN->VIN, GND->GND, BCLK->27, LRC->26, DIN->25
 */

#include "help_sound.h"     // the embedded "Help!" audio (24000 Hz mono PCM)

// ---------------- WIRING CONFIG ----------------
// If your LRC ended up on GPIO33 during debugging, set PIN_LRC = 33.
const int PIN_BCLK = 27;
const int PIN_LRC  = 26;    // <- change to 33 if that's where your wire is
const int PIN_DIN  = 25;
const int BAUD     = 115200;

int  volume   = 13;         // 0..21 (13 = clean on small speakers)
bool loopMode = false;

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------
// I2S setup — auto-detects esp32 core v2 vs v3
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#if defined(ESP_ARDUINO_VERSION_MAJOR) && (ESP_ARDUINO_VERSION_MAJOR >= 3)
  #include <ESP_I2S.h>
  I2SClass i2s;
  void i2sInit() {
    i2s.setPins(PIN_BCLK, PIN_LRC, PIN_DIN);
    i2s.begin(I2S_MODE_STD, HELP_SAMPLE_RATE, I2S_DATA_BIT_WIDTH_16BIT, I2S_SLOT_MODE_MONO);
  }
  void i2sWriteSamples(int16_t *buf, int count) {
    i2s.write((uint8_t *)buf, count * sizeof(int16_t));
  }
#else
  #include <driver/i2s.h>
  void i2sInit() {
    i2s_config_t cfg = {
      .mode = (i2s_mode_t)(I2S_MODE_MASTER | I2S_MODE_TX),
      .sample_rate = HELP_SAMPLE_RATE,
      .bits_per_sample = I2S_BITS_PER_SAMPLE_16BIT,
      .channel_format = I2S_CHANNEL_FMT_ONLY_LEFT,
      .communication_format = I2S_COMM_FORMAT_STAND_I2S,
      .intr_alloc_flags = 0,
      .dma_buf_count = 8,
      .dma_buf_len = 64,
      .use_apll = false,
      .tx_desc_auto_clear = true
    };
    i2s_pin_config_t pins = {
      .mck_io_num = I2S_PIN_NO_CHANGE,
      .bck_io_num = PIN_BCLK,
      .ws_io_num = PIN_LRC,
      .data_out_num = PIN_DIN,
      .data_in_num = I2S_PIN_NO_CHANGE
    };
    i2s_driver_install(I2S_NUM_0, &cfg, 0, NULL);
    i2s_set_pin(I2S_NUM_0, &pins);
  }
  void i2sWriteSamples(int16_t *buf, int count) {
    size_t written = 0;
    i2s_write(I2S_NUM_0, buf, count * sizeof(int16_t), &written, portMAX_DELAY);
  }
#endif

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------
// Voice playback
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------
void playHelp() {
  const int FADE = 72;                       // ~3 ms at 24 kHz
  int16_t buf[256];
  uint32_t pos = 0;
  while (pos < HELP_NUM_SAMPLES) {
    int n = (HELP_NUM_SAMPLES - pos < 256) ? (HELP_NUM_SAMPLES - pos) : 256;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
      uint32_t idx = pos + i;
      int env = volume;
      if (idx < FADE)                        env = volume * idx / FADE;
      if (idx >= HELP_NUM_SAMPLES - FADE)    env = volume * (HELP_NUM_SAMPLES - idx) / FADE;
      int32_t s = ((int32_t)HELP_PCM[idx] * env) / 21;
      buf[i] = (int16_t)s;
    }
    i2sWriteSamples(buf, n);
    pos += n;
  }
}

void playHelpTwice() {
  playHelp();
  delay(400);
  playHelp();
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------
// Beep fallback
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------
int16_t SINE256[256];

void buildSine() {
  for (int i = 0; i < 256; i++)
    SINE256[i] = (int16_t)(32767.0 * sinf(6.28318530718 * i / 256.0));
}

void playTone(int freqHz, int ms) {
  uint32_t step  = (uint32_t)(((double)freqHz * 4294967296.0) / HELP_SAMPLE_RATE);
  uint32_t phase = 0;
  long total = (long)HELP_SAMPLE_RATE * ms / 1000;
  long fade  = HELP_SAMPLE_RATE / 50;
  if (fade * 2 > total) fade = total / 2;
  int16_t buf[64];
  long sent = 0;
  while (sent < total) {
    int n = 64;
    if (sent + n > total) n = (int)(total - sent);
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
      long idx = sent + i;
      int env = volume;
      if (idx < fade)                env = volume * idx / fade;
      else if (idx >= total - fade)  env = volume * (total - idx) / fade;
      int32_t s = ((int32_t)SINE256[phase >> 24] * env) / 21;
      buf[i] = (int16_t)s;
      phase += step;
    }
    i2sWriteSamples(buf, n);
    sent += n;
  }
}

void playChime() {
  playTone(880, 150);  delay(120);
  playTone(880, 150);  delay(120);
  playTone(440, 450);
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------
void handleChar(char c) {
  if (c == '\r' || c == '\n' || c == ' ') return;
  if (c == 'h' || c == 'H') { Serial.println(">> 'Help!'"); playHelp(); }
  else if (c == '2')        { Serial.println(">> 'Help! Help!'"); playHelpTwice(); }
  else if (c == 'l' || c == 'L') {
    loopMode = !loopMode;
    Serial.println(loopMode ? ">> loop ON" : ">> loop OFF");
  }
  else if (c == '+') { if (volume < 21) volume++; Serial.print(">> volume "); Serial.println(volume); }
  else if (c == '-') { if (volume > 0)  volume--; Serial.print(">> volume "); Serial.println(volume); }
  else if (c == 'b' || c == 'B') { Serial.println(">> beep"); playChime(); }
}

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(BAUD);
  delay(800);
  Serial.println();
  Serial.println("VocalBridge — SPEAKER SAYS 'HELP!'");
  Serial.println("----------------------------------");
  i2sInit();
  buildSine();
  Serial.println(">> Saying 'Help!' in 2 seconds — LISTEN...");
  delay(2000);
  playHelp();
}

void loop() {
  static unsigned long lastLoop = 0;
  if (loopMode && millis() - lastLoop >= 3000) {
    lastLoop = millis();
    Serial.println("'Help!' (loop mode)");
    playHelp();
  }
  if (Serial.available()) handleChar(Serial.read());
  delay(10);
}

But it still nakes no change. Everything is excatly the same



Thought for 14 seconds

The user says: "But it still makes no change. Everything is exactly the same."

So after re-uploading the new code (with the 256-step sine), the sound is still the same — same garbling/raspiness, no improvement. That's actually diagnostic gold:

If the code change from a 16-step staircase to a 256-step smooth sine makes NO audible difference whatsoever, then the distortion is NOT from the waveform synthesis — it's from something physical/electrical that's clipping, corrupting, or adding noise to the signal path. A 16x improvement in waveform quality should be clearly audible. "Exactly the same" means the garble dominates from another source.

What could cause identical garble regardless of waveform quality?

Clipping/overdrive in the amp — but I lowered volume default from 10 (SpeakerTest starts at 10)... wait, SpeakerTest always started at volume=10. Hmm, actually in SpeakerTest v1 default was 10; the updated one also 10. SayHelp went 18→13. If they're testing SpeakerTest, volume unchanged at 10. And they may not have sent -. But would clipping sound "the same" for both waveforms? Clipping squares off the tops — a clipped sine sounds like a buzzy square wave. A 16-step sine ALREADY sounds like a buzzy approximation. So yes — if the amp is clipping at volume 10, both would sound similarly harsh! The envelope scaling: my volume math — ((int32_t)SINE256[...] * env)/21 with env=10: max = 32767*10/21 = 15603. Hmm that's not clipping the DAC (max 32767). But the MAX98357A gain default is 9dB with 3W into 4Ω... at full DAC scale it'd be loud. We're at ~48% DAC scale. Shouldn't clip the amp itself... unless VIN is 5V and speaker is 4Ω — fine.

Also the "What is LRC" question — explain simply:

I2S ships audio like a conveyor belt of small boxes (samples), one box per tick of BCLK. But the amp needs to know: where does a number START and END? Is this 16-bit number the LEFT or RIGHT channel? LRC (aka WS, word select / left-right clock) is the "frame flag" that toggles: LOW = left channel's bits coming, HIGH = right channel's bits coming. Without it, the amp can't find the boundaries between numbers — it reads bits shifted by 1, 3, 7... bits → garbage values → the exact raspy noise they heard with LRC dangling. That's why the garble "changed with the audio" — data was arriving, just mis-sliced. Nice concrete tie-in: "you already heard what missing LRC sounds like."

Analogy: BCLK = the ticking metronome; DIN = someone reading digits aloud; LRC = the person raising their hand at the start of each new number. Without the raised hand you hear digits but can't tell where one number ends and the next begins.

Good question — and understanding LRC actually explains a lot of what you've heard. Let me answer that first, then tackle the soldering result.

What LRC actually does 🧠
I2S ships audio as a stream of bits — but bits have no labels. The amp receives a river of 1s and 0s and needs to know: where does one number end and the next begin?

Wire	Job	Analogy
BCLK	tick… tick… tick — one bit per tick	the metronome
DIN	the actual bits (the audio numbers)	someone reading digits aloud
LRC	raises a flag at the start of each new number (low = left channel, high = right)	raising a hand at the start of each number
Without LRC, the amp hears all the digits but can't tell where numbers start — so it slices the bit-river at the wrong offsets, turning perfectly good audio into garbage values. That's literally the raspy noise you heard with LRC dangling — data was arriving, just mis-sliced. When you fixed LRC, the tune appeared through the noise — the slicing got right, but something is still mangling the signal itself.

Biquad high-shelf (RBJ cookbook): A = 10^(dB/40); w0 = 2π f0/Fs; alpha = sin(w0)/2Q (shelf uses Q too per RBJ: alpha = sin(w0)/2 * sqrt((A+1/A)*(1/S-1)+2) with S=shelf slope; simpler: use Q form). High-pass biquad (RBJ): b0 = (1+cos)/2, b1 = -(1+cos), b2 = (1+cos)/2, a0 = 1+α, a1 = -2cos, a2 = 1-α, α = sin/(2Q).

python


def time_stretch(xs, ratio, fs, grain_ms=22, search_ms=8):
    # WSOLA-lite: Hann-windowed grains, output hop = input hop / ratio... 
Wait, direction: ratio = how much LONGER the output is (1.12 = 12% slower).

Implementation (standard OLA):

N = grain samples (e.g., int(0.022*fs) ≈ 528)
Analysis hop Ha = N // 2
Synthesis hop Hs = int(Ha * ratio) — wait no. Let me think again.*
OLA time-stretch: we read input grains at analysis positions advancing by Ha, and write them to output advancing by Hs. Output length = input length × (Hs/Ha)... no wait:

If input advances by Ha per grain and output advances by Hs per grain, then output_len/input_len = Hs/Ha. For STRETCHING (longer output), Hs > Ha? No! If we place grains FURTHER apart in the output than we found them in input, output is longer. Hs/Ha = ratio > 1 → Hs = Ha * ratio. Hmm wait: input span = num_grains * Ha ≈ input_len. Output span = num_grains * Hs ≈ input_len * (Hs/Ha) = input_len * ratio. Yes: Hs = int(Haratio), ratio 1.12.

With 50% overlap Hann grains and WSOLA alignment (shift analysis position within ±search to maximize cross-correlation with the existing output tail), quality is good.

WSOLA-lite in pure Python:

python


def time_stretch(xs, ratio, fs, grain_ms=22.0, search_ms=6.0):
    N = int(grain_ms * fs / 1000)
    Ha = N // 2
    Hs = int(round(Ha * ratio))
    S = int(search_ms * fs / 1000)
    win = [0.5 - 0.5*math.cos(2*math.pi*i/N) for i in range(N)]
    out = [0.0] * (int(len(xs) * ratio) + N)
    n_grains = (len(xs) - N) // Ha
    synth_pos = 0
    for g in range(n_grains):
        ideal = g * Ha
        # first grain: no alignment
        if g == 0:
            ana = ideal
        else:
            # align grain start so its beginning matches output content at synth_pos
            best, bestscore = ideal, -1e18
            lo, hi = max(0, ideal - S), min(len(xs) - N, ideal + S)
            for cand in range(lo, hi, 2):  # step 2 for speed
                score = 0.0
                for k in range(0, N, 8):   # sparse correlation
                    score += xs[cand + k] * out[synth_pos + k]
                if score > bestscore:
                    bestscore, best = score, cand
            ana = best
        for i in range(N):
            out[synth_pos + i] += xs[ana + i] * win[i]
        synth_pos += Hs
    # normalize for the 50%-overlap Hann sum (≈1.0 for COLA... with stretch Hs≠Ha it's not perfect COLA; rescale by window sum)
    # compute actual amplitude envelope and flatten: simpler — divide by accumulated window
    ...
Hmm, with Hs ≠ Ha the Hann overlap-add isn't constant (Hs = 1.12 * N/2). The window sum varies periodically → amplitude modulation artifacts. Better approach: use synthesis window BOTH sides (grain windowed at analysis AND divide output by summed squared windows) — standard weighted-OLA: out[i] = Σ w[n]x[n] / Σ w[n]... For robustness: accumulate window sum array wsum, then out[i] /= max(wsum[i], eps). With Hann on analysis only and dividing by accumulated window sum, the COLA issue disappears.*

So:

python


wsum = [0.0]*len(out)
... out[synth_pos+i] += xs[ana+i]*win[i]; wsum[synth_pos+i] += win[i]
... final: out[i] = out[i]/wsum[i] where wsum[i] > 0.01 else 0
That's clean weighted OLA.

Complexity: n_grains ≈ (10500-528)/264 ≈ 38 grains; each search ~ (2*144/2=144 candidates) × (528/8=66 mults) ≈ 9.5k ops → 38 × 9.5k ≈ 360k — trivial.

The sparse cross-correlation with out[] tail — note out tail beyond current synth_pos contains data from previous grains (overlap region) — that's exactly what we correlate against. synth_pos+k for k in 0..N: out has data up to previous synth_pos + N = synth_pos + Ha... since previous grain wrote prev_synth, prev_synth+N) and synth_pos = prev_synth + Hs, and Hs > Ha slightly (264*1.12=296): out[synth_pos + k] valid for k < N - (Hs - Ha) = N - 32 ≈ 496. Correlating the full N could read zeros — harmless (correlation just weaker there). Fine. Actually limit k to N//2 for speed and validity. [blocked]

Edge case: wsum small at edges → fade edges.

OK, and the compression stage v2:

python


g = 10**(8.0/20)   # +8 dB
knee = 0.5
for x in xs:
    x *= g
    a = abs(x)
    if a > knee: a = knee + (1-knee)*math.tanh((a-knee)/(1-knee))
    out = copysign(a, x)
Hmm previous: knee 0.75, (1-knee)=0.25, tanh((a-0.75)/0.25). Generalize: above knee, soft-map to knee..1. This is heavy compression — speech RMS will approach maybe -10..-11 dBFS. Then normalize 0.99.

Also — safety: heavy limiting can sound "pumpy/squashed" — for a 0.44s "Help!" it's fine, punchy even.

Option B: Better stretching algorithm. The current WSOLA is my own crude implementation. I could improve it substantially:

The issue: at ratio 3, Ha = N//2 = 180 samples (7.5ms hop at 24kHz)... wait N=30ms=720 samples, Ha=360 (15ms hop), Hs=1080 (45ms synth hop). The analysis hop is fixed at Ha while synthesis hops at Hs=3×Ha. With WSOLA, after the first grain, each subsequent grain must search ±S (12ms) around the ideal position to find best correlation with the already-written output. At high ratios the ideal positions march along the source faster than natural continuation... my search normalization and range might be insufficient; also searching only every 2 samples with step 4 correlation is coarse.
A classic better approach: phase vocoder — for speech it can sound phasey/reverberant too unless phase-locked. Hmm.

Better practical option: hybrid — moderate WSOLA + moderate sample-rate... no, pitch must stay.

python


def fft(a):  # iterative radix-2, in-place style, returns complex list
    n = len(a)  # power of 2
    # bit reversal
    j = 0
    for i in range(1, n):
        bit = n >> 1
        while j & bit: j ^= bit; bit >>= 1
        j |= bit
        if i < j: a[i], a[j] = a[j], a[i]
    length = 2
    while length <= n:
        ang = -2*math.pi/length
        wr, wi = math.cos(ang), math.sin(ang)
        for i in range(0, n, length):
            cr, ci = 1.0, 0.0
            for k in range(i, i+length//2):
                ur, ui = a[k].real, a[k].imag
                vr = a[k+length//2].real*cr - a[k+length//2].imag*ci
                vi = a[k+length//2].real*ci + a[k+length//2].imag*cr
                a[k] = complex(ur+vr, ui+vi)
                a[k+length//2] = complex(ur-vr, ui-vi)
                cr, ci = cr*wr-ci*wi, cr*wi+ci*wr
        length <<= 1
    return a
Performance: N=1024, ~94 frames × 2 (forward) + 94 inverse = ~200 FFTs of 1024. Each FFT ~ N/2 * log2(N) butterflies = 51210 = 5120 butterflies, each ~10 flops → 50k ops per FFT → 10M ops total in pure Python… ~5-15 seconds. Acceptable.

PV algorithm:

N=1024, hopA=256 (75% overlap), Hann.
Precompute window.
Frames: for t in range(0, len(x)-N+1, hopA): frame = x[t:t+N]*win; X = fft(frame); store mag & phase arrays.
Initialize prev_phase = phases[0], out_phase = phases[0] copy? Standard init: sum_phase = phases[0].
For each frame i>0:
for each bin k: delta = princarg(phase[i][k] - phase[i-1][k] - 2πk·hopA/N); omega = 2πk/N + delta/hopA; out_phase[k] += omega*hopS (accumulate)
Actually accumulate: sum_phase[k] = sum_phase[k] + omega[k]*hopS, where omega computed from analysis phases.
Peak locking (identity): find peaks in mag[i] (local maxima above threshold); for each peak p, compute rotation = sum_phase[p] - phase[i][p] (the phase advance correction); for bins in region (from previous peak+1 to next peak... typically region around p: [prev_peak+1 .. p] and (p .. next_peak] midpoint boundaries), set their sum_phase such that relative phases are preserved: out_phase[k] = phase[i][k] + rotation for k in region. This is "identity phase locking" (Laroche & Dolson).
Synthesis frame: Y[k] = mag[i][k] * exp(i·out_phase[k]); y_frame = ifft(Y); overlap-add y_framewin at synthesis position ihopS; also accumulate win² for normalization.
Normalize: y[t] /= win_sum[t] where win_sum > epsilon.
Result length ≈ (num_frames-1)*hopS + N.
princarg(x) = (x + π) mod 2π - π.

hopS = round(hopA * ratio). For ratio 2.8: hopS = 717 (round). Actual ratio = 717/256 = 2.801.*

analysis hop Ha, synthesis hop Hs.
For frame n: phases φn[k].

Peak locking (Laroche-Dolson "identity"):

Find peaks in mag[n].
For each peak index p: Δθ[p] = θ[p] − φn[p] (rotation needed at peak).
For bins between peaks (region = (prev_p, p]): θ[k] = φn[k] + Δθ[p] where p is the peak governing that region — governs up to midpoint between peaks typically; simple version: region boundaries at midpoints between adjacent peaks. Implementation: for each bin k, find its governing peak (the nearest peak index). θ[k] = φn[k] + Δθ[gov(k)].
That's straightforward. Peaks: k is a peak if mag[k] > mag[k-1] and mag[k] > mag[k+1] and mag[k] > small threshold.

The "help me" variant is worth a real listen — "Help me!" is what people actually shout, the delivery is naturally more desperate, and it needed less stretching.

How the words got slower (without cackle)
The phase vocoder doesn't cut-and-paste grains (that's what warbled). It converts the voice to frequencies + phases, slows the phase evolution, and rebuilds the audio — so pitch, timbre, and the voice's identity stay put while the words take their time. This is the industry-standard method for exactly this job.

On a tiny speaker with a 300 Hz HPF, "Help" loses the low fundamentals of the vowel — the vowel /ɛ/ has energy 400-2000 Hz (fine), but the consonants: /h/ is breath (high freq, quiet), /l/ is weak, /p/ is a short plosive burst. "Help" through a small speaker = mostly vowel + weak consonants. Hard to identify cold.

The stretch (1.8×) smears the consonants. Phase vocoder stretching transient consonants (p, t, k) smears them — attacks get soft. That hurts intelligibility significantly. A natural-speed word has crisp transients.

The user has discovered a classic speech intelligibility problem: the word "HELP" ends in /lp/ — a liquid + stop consonant cluster. The final /p/ is a voiceless stop: it's basically a tiny burst of air (plosive) that's very low energy. Also, their emphasis attempts sound "unpleasing" — over-emphasized articulation sounds strained/unnatural.

You CAN do dual-OTA on smaller flash (2 MB would be tight but possible with minimal partitions; e.g. two 640 KB app partitions + spiffs on 2 MB). But practically, 4 MB is the standard devkit flash and the safe statement. Mostly true in practice.

"Rollback Safety: if the update fails mid-air, the target cancels and safely reboots back to original code" — TRUE with a caveat: this requires designing it right. The OTA scheme inherently keeps the old image in the other partition until the new one boots; the rollback feature (app rollback / CONFIG_BOOTLOADER_APP_ROLLBACK_ENABLE) marks images pending-verify. /*
 * VocalBridge Final_V1 — SPEAKER SAYS WORDS (your own voice)
 * -----------------------------------------------------------
 * Two words on-chip, in YOUR voice: HELP and WATER.
 * No SD card, no DFPlayer. More words = record + make_word_header.py.
 *
 * Board:  ESP32 Dev Module        Baud: 115200
 * Library: NONE (esp32 core v2.x and v3.x auto-detected)
 *
 * WIRING (same as always):
 *   MAX98357A  VIN->VIN(5V)  GND->GND  BCLK->GPIO27  LRC->GPIO26  DIN->GPIO25
 *   Speaker -> + / -  (SOLDER the joints - twist joints garble the bass)
 *
 * COMMANDS (Serial Monitor 115200):
 *   h    say "HELP!"          w    say "WATER!"
 *   b    beep chime           l    loop HELP every 3 s (filming)
 *   + -  volume               i    info
 *
 * HOW TO ADD MORE WORDS (YES / NO / PAIN ...):
 *   1. Record the word (quiet room, phone 15-20 cm, natural calling pace)
 *   2. Convert to WAV, then: python3 make_word_header.py recording.wav YES
 *   3. Put YES_voice.h in this folder, add #include "yes_voice.h" below,
 *      copy one playWord() block, pick a key. Done.
 */

#include "help_voice.h"     // your voice: HELP  x2
#include "water_voice.h"    // your voice: WATER x2

// ---------------- WIRING CONFIG ----------------
const int PIN_BCLK = 27;
const int PIN_LRC  = 26;
const int PIN_DIN  = 25;
const int BAUD     = 115200;

int  volume   = 15;         // 0..21
bool loopMode = false;

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------
// I2S — auto-detects esp32 core v2 vs v3
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#if defined(ESP_ARDUINO_VERSION_MAJOR) && (ESP_ARDUINO_VERSION_MAJOR >= 3)
  #include <ESP_I2S.h>
  I2SClass i2s;
  void i2sInit() {
    i2s.setPins(PIN_BCLK, PIN_LRC, PIN_DIN);
    i2s.begin(I2S_MODE_STD, 24000, I2S_DATA_BIT_WIDTH_16BIT, I2S_SLOT_MODE_MONO);
  }
  void i2sWriteSamples(int16_t *buf, int count) {
    i2s.write((uint8_t *)buf, count * sizeof(int16_t));
  }
#else
  #include <driver/i2s.h>
  void i2sInit() {
    i2s_config_t cfg = {
      .mode = (i2s_mode_t)(I2S_MODE_MASTER | I2S_MODE_TX),
      .sample_rate = 24000,
      .bits_per_sample = I2S_BITS_PER_SAMPLE_16BIT,
      .channel_format = I2S_CHANNEL_FMT_ONLY_LEFT,
      .communication_format = I2S_COMM_FORMAT_STAND_I2S,
      .intr_alloc_flags = 0,
      .dma_buf_count = 8,
      .dma_buf_len = 64,
      .use_apll = true,     // precision audio clock
      .tx_desc_auto_clear = true
    };
    i2s_pin_config_t pins = {
      .mck_io_num = I2S_PIN_NO_CHANGE,
      .bck_io_num = PIN_BCLK,
      .ws_io_num = PIN_LRC,
      .data_out_num = PIN_DIN,
      .data_in_num = I2S_PIN_NO_CHANGE
    };
    if (i2s_driver_install(I2S_NUM_0, &cfg, 0, NULL) != ESP_OK) {
      cfg.use_apll = false;
      i2s_driver_install(I2S_NUM_0, &cfg, 0, NULL);
    }
    i2s_set_pin(I2S_NUM_0, &pins);
  }
  void i2sWriteSamples(int16_t *buf, int count) {
    size_t written = 0;
    i2s_write(I2S_NUM_0, buf, count * sizeof(int16_t), &written, portMAX_DELAY);
  }
#endif

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------
// Generic word playback (any voice header works)
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------
void playClip(const int16_t *pcm, uint32_t n, uint32_t rate) {
  const int FADE = 72;
  int16_t buf[256];
  uint32_t pos = 0;
  while (pos < n) {
    uint32_t chunk = (n - pos < 256) ? (n - pos) : 256;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < chunk; i++) {
      uint32_t idx = pos + i;
      int env = volume;
      if (idx < FADE)               env = volume * idx / FADE;
      if (idx >= n - FADE)          env = volume * (n - idx) / FADE;
      int32_t s = ((int32_t)pcm[idx] * env) / 21;
      buf[i] = (int16_t)s;
    }
    i2sWriteSamples(buf, chunk);
    pos += chunk;
  }
}

// 2-beep alarm intro (attention-grabber before the word)
int16_t SINE256[256];
void buildSine() {
  for (int i = 0; i < 256; i++)
    SINE256[i] = (int16_t)(32767.0 * sinf(6.28318530718 * i / 256.0));
}
void playTone(int freqHz, int ms) {
  uint32_t step = (uint32_t)(((double)freqHz * 4294967296.0) / 24000);
  uint32_t phase = 0;
  long total = 24000L * ms / 1000;
  long fade = 24000 / 50;
  if (fade * 2 > total) fade = total / 2;
  int16_t buf[64]; long sent = 0;
  while (sent < total) {
    int nn = 64;
    if (sent + nn > total) nn = (int)(total - sent);
    for (int i = 0; i < nn; i++) {
      long idx = sent + i;
      int env = volume;
      if (idx < fade)              env = volume * idx / fade;
      else if (idx >= total - fade) env = volume * (total - idx) / fade;
      int32_t s = ((int32_t)SINE256[phase >> 24] * env) / 21;
      buf[i] = (int16_t)s;
      phase += step;
    }
    i2sWriteSamples(buf, nn);
    sent += nn;
  }
}
void playAlertBeeps() {
  playTone(1760, 110); delay(90);
  playTone(1760, 110); delay(220);
}

void sayHELP()  { playAlertBeeps(); playClip(HELP_PCM,  HELP_NUM_SAMPLES,  HELP_SAMPLE_RATE); }
void sayWATER() { playAlertBeeps(); playClip(WATER_PCM, WATER_NUM_SAMPLES, WATER_SAMPLE_RATE); }

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------
void printHelp() {
  Serial.println();
  Serial.println("------------- SPEAKER SAYS WORDS — commands -------------");
  Serial.println("  h   say 'HELP!'         w   say 'WATER!'");
  Serial.println("  b   beep                l   loop HELP every 3 s");
  Serial.println("  + / -  volume           i   info");
  Serial.println("----------------------------------------------------------");
  Serial.println();
}

void handleChar(char c) {
  if (c == '\r' || c == '\n' || c == ' ') return;
  if (c == 'h' || c == 'H') { Serial.println(">> 'HELP!'");  sayHELP(); }
  else if (c == 'w' || c == 'W') { Serial.println(">> 'WATER!'"); sayWATER(); }
  else if (c == 'b' || c == 'B') { Serial.println(">> beep"); playTone(880, 150); delay(120); playTone(440, 450); }
  else if (c == 'l' || c == 'L') {
    loopMode = !loopMode;
    Serial.println(loopMode ? ">> loop ON" : ">> loop OFF");
  }
  else if (c == '+') { if (volume < 21) volume++; Serial.print(">> volume "); Serial.println(volume); }
  else if (c == '-') { if (volume > 0)  volume--; Serial.print(">> volume "); Serial.println(volume); }
  else if (c == 'i' || c == 'I') {
    Serial.print(">> HELP: ");  Serial.print(HELP_VOICE_VERSION);
    Serial.print(" | WATER: "); Serial.println(WATER_VOICE_VERSION);
  }
  else { Serial.print("?? '"); Serial.write(c); Serial.println("'"); }
}

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(BAUD);
  delay(800);
  Serial.println();
  Serial.println("VocalBridge Final_V1 — SPEAKER SAYS WORDS (your own voice)");
  Serial.println("----------------------------------------------------------");
  Serial.print("HELP  : ");  Serial.println(HELP_VOICE_VERSION);
  Serial.print("WATER : ");  Serial.println(WATER_VOICE_VERSION);
  Serial.print("COMPILED: "); Serial.print(__DATE__); Serial.print(" "); Serial.println(__TIME__);
  i2sInit();
  buildSine();
  printHelp();
  Serial.println(">> Saying 'HELP!' in 2 seconds — LISTEN...");
  delay(2000);
  sayHELP();
}

void loop() {
  static unsigned long lastLoop = 0;
  if (loopMode && millis() - lastLoop >= 3000) {
    lastLoop = millis();
    Serial.println("'HELP!' (loop mode)");
    sayHELP();
  }
  if (Serial.available()) handleChar(Serial.read());
  delay(10);
}

python


import re
def parse(path):
    txt = open(path).read()
    m = re.search(r"NUM_SAMPLES = (\d+)", txt)
    n = int(m.group(1))
    m = re.search(r"PCM\[\] = \{(.*?)\};", txt, re.S)
    pcm = [int(x) for x in m.group(1).replace("\n","").split(",") if x.strip()]
    return n, pcm

The full python verify script:

python


import re, subprocess, sys
def parse(txt):
    n = int(re.search(r"NUM_SAMPLES = (\d+)", txt).group(1))
    body = re.search(r"PCM\[\] = \{(.*?)\};", txt, re.S).group(1)
    pcm = [int(x) for x in body.replace("\n","").split(",") if x.strip()]
    return n, pcm
GAP = 5280
ok = True
for w in ["help","water","yes","no"]:
    old = subprocess.run(["git","show","HEAD:SpeakerSayWords_MAX98357A/%s_voice.h"%w],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout
    new = open("SpeakerSayWords_MAX98357A/%s_voice.h"%w).read()
    n_old, p_old = parse(old); n_new, p_new = parse(new)
    N = (n_old-GAP)//2
    c1 = n_old == 2*N+GAP
    c2 = p_old[N:N+GAP] == [0]*GAP
    c3 = p_old[:N] == p_old[N+GAP:]
    c4 = n_new == N and p_new == p_old[:N]
    print(w.upper(), "old=%d new=%d dur=%.2fs"%(n_old,n_new,n_new/24000), "gap-zero:%s dup-exact:%s new==first-copy:%s"%(c2,c3,c4))
    ok = ok and c1 and c2 and c3 and c4
print("ALL BIT-EXACT" if ok else "FAIL")
sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

Sketch details — let me now write it:

cpp


/*
 * VocalBridge — SENSE WORDS (data recording, NO deciding)
 * ...banner philosophy: this sketch only SHOWS muscle electricity.
 * Board: ESP32 Dev Module, baud 115200
 * WIRING (AD8232): OUT->GPIO34, LO+->GPIO32, LO-->GPIO33, 3V3->3V3(+), GND->GND(-)
 * No speaker, no amp needed for this test.
 */
const int PIN_OUT = 34;  // AD8232 OUT (ADC1_CH6, input-only pin)
const int PIN_LOP = 32;  // LO+
const int PIN_LON = 33;  // LO-
Sampling: SAMPLE_MS=2 (500 Hz), PRINT_MS=50 (20 Hz). ENV decay 0.97/sample. Center EMA alpha 0.001. Peak ring 200 ms.

pads: (digitalRead(LOP)==HIGH || digitalRead(LON)==HIGH) → off. Note: on some AD8232 boards, LO detection needs pull-ups configured; the SparkFun hook guide: LO+ LO− directly to digital pins, HIGH = leads off. pinMode INPUT. ✓ (matches prior demo wiring.)

Print format:



Serial.print("raw:"); Serial.print(raw);
Serial.print(",env:"); Serial.print(env);
Serial.print(",peak:"); Serial.print(peak);
Serial.print(",pads:"); Serial.print(padsOn ? 1 : 0);
Serial.print("  [t="); Serial.print(millis()/1000.0, 2); Serial.println("s]");
Float print every line (20 Hz) ok.

Marks: on 'h' → print >>>MARK:HELP t=12.34s<<< (matching their word keys h/w/y/n! consistent with speaker sketch muscle memory ✓). 's' → >>>MARK:SILENT(no word) t=...<<<. Any other char → reprint quick help (plotter-safe lines).

Also maybe 'q' = quiet banner toggle? Unneeded.

Also: should the data line include leads-off ALERT text when pads:0? e.g. append CHECK-PADS! when off — chunks "CHECK-PADS!" NaN ✓ safe. Do it: visible in monitor; plotter unaffected.

Env peak ring: store env in circular buffer size 100 (200 ms @ 500 Hz); peak = max. Simple.

Center: initialize center=raw on first sample.

Handle ADC setup for both cores: analogReadResolution(12); analogSetPinAttenuation(PIN_OUT, ADC_11db); — core v3 supports these APIs ✓ (analogSetPinAttenuation exists in v3? In v3, analogSetAttenuation / analogSetPinAttenuation — yes still available via Arduino ESP32 API. ✓)

Loop structure:

cpp


void loop() {
  // sample every 2 ms
  if (millis() - tS >= 2) { tS += 2; sample(); }
  // print every 50 ms
  if (millis() - tP >= 50) { tP += 50; printLine(); }
  // serial marks
  while (Serial.available()) handleKey(Serial.read());
}
sample(): raw=analogRead; center += 0.001*(raw-center); dev=abs(raw-center); env = dev>env? dev : env0.97; ring update. printLine(): compute peak from ring, pads, print.

Edge: tS += 2 drift vs millis catchup — fine.

Where to put the pads (AD8232, speech sensing)

cpp


/*
 * VocalBridge — SENSE WORDS  (SenseWords_AD8232)
 * ------------------------------------------------
 * DATA RECORDING ONLY. This sketch never decides what word was said.
 * It only shows the electricity your speech muscles make, so we can
 * look at the readings together (you film Serial Monitor + Plotter).
 *
 * Board: ESP32 Dev Module     Baud: 115200
 * No speaker / amp needed. Sensor only.
 *
 * WIRING (AD8232):
 *   3V3 -> 3V3    GND -> GND
 *   OUT -> GPIO34   LO+ -> GPIO32   LO- -> GPIO33
 *
 * PLOTTER (Arduino IDE 2): four curves — raw, env, peak, pads.
 * MONITOR: same numbers + timestamp. MARK keys:
 *   h=HELP  w=WATER  y=YES  n=NO  s=silent  r=fast/slow  i=info
 */
Wait — banner comments in .ino source are fine (never printed). The PRINTED banner must be plotter-safe. Code comments can have anything.

cpp


const int PIN_OUT = 34;
const int PIN_LOP = 32;
const int PIN_LON = 33;
const int SAMPLE_MS = 2;     // 500 Hz internal sampling
int printMs = 50;            // 20 lines/s (press r for slow)
long center = 2048;          // slow baseline (auto-follows drift)
int  env = 0;                // peak-hold envelope of muscle burst
const int RING = 100;        // ~200 ms of envelope history
int ring[RING]; int ringIdx = 0;
bool firstSample = true;
unsigned long tS = 0, tP = 0;
void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);
  pinMode(PIN_LOP, INPUT);
  pinMode(PIN_LON, INPUT);
  analogReadResolution(12);
  analogSetPinAttenuation(PIN_OUT, ADC_11db);
  delay(800);
  printBanner();
}

  Serial.println();
  Serial.println(F("==== VocalBridge SENSE-WORDS (record-only, no deciding) ===="));
  Serial.println(F("version=SenseV1   baud=115200"));

  Serial.println(F("plotter: curves raw,env,peak,pads"));
  Serial.println(F("mark keys: h=HELP,w=WATER,y=YES,n=NO,s=silent"));
  Serial.println(F("keys: r=fast/slow lines, i=this info"));
  Serial.println(F("keep face relaxed the first seconds -> baseline settles"));
  Serial.println(F("streaming..."));
}

sample():

cpp


void sample() {
  int raw = analogRead(PIN_OUT);
  if (firstSample) { center = raw; firstSample = false; }
  center += (raw - center) / 1024;          // ~2 s time constant at 500 Hz
  int dev = abs(raw - center);
  if (dev > env) env = dev;
  else env = (env * 97) / 100;              // ~130 ms fall
  ring[ringIdx] = env; ringIdx = (ringIdx + 1) % RING;
}
center += (raw-center)/1024 — integer long math: raw int, center long. (raw - center)/1024 → truncation toward 0 fine. At 500 Hz, tau = 1024/500 ≈ 2 s ✓.

env decay 0.97 per 2 ms → tau ≈ 66 ms → falls 2000→300 in ~4.5 tau ≈ 130*4.5... ln(2000/300)=1.9 tau ≈ 125 ms. Good.

printLine():

cpp


void printLine() {
  int peak = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < RING; i++) if (ring[i] > peak) peak = ring[i];
  bool padsOn = (digitalRead(PIN_LOP) == LOW && digitalRead(PIN_LON) == LOW);
  Serial.print(F("raw:"));   Serial.print(lastRaw);
  Serial.print(F(",env:"));  Serial.print(env);
  Serial.print(F(",peak:")); Serial.print(peak);
  Serial.print(F(",pads:")); Serial.print(padsOn ? 1 : 0);
  Serial.print(F("  [t="));  Serial.print(millis() / 1000.0, 2); Serial.print(F("s]"));
  if (!padsOn) Serial.print(F("  CHECK-PADS!"));
  Serial.println();
}
need lastRaw stored in sample(): add int lastRaw;.

handleKey:

cpp


void handleKey(char c) {
  if (c == '\r' || c == '\n' || c == ' ') return;
  if (c == 'h' || c == 'H') { Serial.print(F(">>>MARK:HELP t=")); ... }
  ... w, y, n ...
  s → ">>>MARK:SILENT t=...s<<<"
  r → toggle printMs 50/250, print ">>>rate=slow..." 
  i → printBanner()
  else → short help line
}
Marks print: Serial.print(millis()/1000.0, 2) then "s<<<".

loop():

cpp


void loop() {
  unsigned long now = millis();
  if (now - tS >= (unsigned long)SAMPLE_MS) { tS = now; sample(); }
  if (now - tP >= (unsigned long)printMs)   { tP = now; printLine(); }
  while (Serial.available()) handleKey(Serial.read());
}

Pad placement — speech muscle recording (AD8232)

const unsigned long MIN_BURST_MS = 200; // must be present this long
unsigned long presenceStart = 0;
bool presence = false;
in loop, per sample-ish (2ms cadence — but our loop runs every loop() iteration, and detection block runs every loop; env updates at 2ms):
if (env >= PRESENCE_LVL) {
  if (!presence) { presence = true; presenceStart = now; }
  if (env >= thresh && !firedThisBurst && now - presenceStart >= MIN_BURST_MS && now - lastFire >= REFRACTORY_MS) {
    fire; lastFire = now; firedThisBurst = true; burstPeak=0;
  }
} else {
  presence = false; firedThisBurst = false; burstPeak = 0;
}

I'll write:


void runCalibrate() {
  Serial.println(F(">>> CALIBRATE: sit SILENT + STILL for 5 s..."));
  const int N = 100;
  int buf[N];
  for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
    unsigned long st = millis();
    while (millis() - st < 50) { sample(); delay(2); }
    buf[i] = env;
  }
  // sort
  for (int i = 0; i < N - 1; i++) for (int j = i + 1; j < N; j++) if (buf[j] < buf[i]) { int tmp = buf[i]; buf[i] = buf[j]; buf[j] = tmp; }
  int med = (buf[N/2 - 1] + buf[N/2]) / 2;
  burstLvl = med + 200;
  thresh  = med + 350;
  inBurst = false; burstPeak = 0;   // reset detector state
  Serial.print(F(">>> CALIBRATE done. silence=")); Serial.print(med);
  Serial.print(F("  burst=")); Serial.print(burstLvl);
  Serial.print(F("  alert=")); Serial.println(thresh);
  Serial.println(F(">>> if you talked during calibration, press c again"));
}

/*
 * VocalBridge — HELP DETECTOR (HelpDetect_AD8232)  V1.4
 * ------------------------------------------------------
 * V1.3 lesson (29 Sep, session 3): the green (RL) electrode moved from
 * below the collarbone to the BACK OF THE NECK. Same voice, same word —
 * but the signal HALVED (words 1556-1764 -> 564-854; silence ~314 -> ~275).
 * Fixed thresholds cannot survive a placement change.
 *
 * V1.4 = CALIBRATION:
 *   - press 'c' while SILENT and STILL: the board measures your silence
 *     level for 5 s and sets both gate levels from it:
 *         burst level = silence + 200   (burst starts here)
 *         alert level = silence + 300   (peak needed to alert)
 *   - alert = peak >= alert level AND burst lasts >= 250 ms (V1.3 shape gate)
 *   - defaults below ship tuned for RL on the BACK OF THE NECK
 *   - +/- still tunes the alert level by 100 if you want it live
 *
 * MEASURED (29 Sep):
 *   RL below collarbone: silence ~314, words 1556-1764 (5x)
 *   RL back of neck    : silence ~275, words 564-854  (2.3x)  <- weaker!
 *
 * Board: ESP32 Dev Module, Baud 115200. Wiring same as always:
 *   AD8232: 3V3->3V3  GND->GND  OUT->GPIO34  LO+->GPIO32  LO-->GPIO33
 *
 * KEYS:  c calibrate (SILENT!)  +/- alert level x100   t test alert
 *        i info   r fast/slow   h/w/y/n/s marks
 */
const int PIN_OUT = 34, PIN_LOP = 32, PIN_LON = 33;
const int SAMPLE_MS = 2;
int printMs = 50;
long center = 2048;
int  env = 0, lastRaw = 0;
bool firstSample = true;
const int RING = 100;
int ring[RING]; int ringIdx = 0;
// ---------- detector V1.4 (shape gate + calibration) ----------
int  thresh  = 575;   // alert level (peak needed) - default: RL back of neck
int  burstLvl = 475;  // burst begins here         - default: RL back of neck
const unsigned long BURST_GRACE_MS = 150;   // dips shorter than this stay in the burst
const unsigned long SPEECH_MIN_MS  = 250;   // burst must LAST this long to alert
const unsigned long REFRACTORY_MS  = 1500;
bool inBurst = false, firedThisBurst = false;
unsigned long burstStart = 0, lastHigh = 0, lastFire = 0;
int  burstPeak = 0, maxEnvEver = 0, helpCount = 0;
unsigned long tS = 0, tP = 0;
void printBanner() { ... V1.4 text ... }
void mark(...) same
void fireHelp(...) same
void reportBurst(...) same
void runCalibrate() {
  Serial.println(F(">>> CALIBRATE: sit SILENT + STILL, do not talk..."));
  const int N = 100;              // 100 x 50 ms = 5 s
  int buf[N];
  for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
    unsigned long st = millis();
    while (millis() - st < 50) { sample(); delay(2); }
    buf[i] = env;
  }
  for (int i = 0; i < N - 1; i++)
    for (int j = i + 1; j < N; j++)
      if (buf[j] < buf[i]) { int tmp = buf[i]; buf[i] = buf[j]; buf[j] = tmp; }
  int med = (buf[N/2 - 1] + buf[N/2]) / 2;
  burstLvl = med + 200;
  thresh   = med + 300;
  inBurst = false; burstPeak = 0; firedThisBurst = false;
  Serial.print(F(">>> CALIBRATE done. silence=")); Serial.print(med);
  Serial.print(F("  burst="));  Serial.print(burstLvl);
  Serial.print(F("  alert="));  Serial.println(thresh);
  Serial.println(F(">>> if you talked during it, press c again"));
}

/*
 * VocalBridge — HELP DETECTOR (HelpDetect_AD8232)  V1.4
 * ------------------------------------------------------
 * V1.3 lesson (29 Sep, session 3): the green (RL) electrode moved from
 * below the collarbone to the BACK OF THE NECK. Same voice, same word,
 * but the signal HALVED (words 1556-1764 -> 564-854). Fixed thresholds
 * cannot survive a placement change.
 *
 * V1.4 = CALIBRATION + V1.3 shape gate:
 *   - press 'c' while SILENT and STILL: the board measures your silence
 *     level for 5 s and sets both gate levels from it:
 *         burst level = silence + 200   (a burst starts here)
 *         alert level = silence + 300   (peak needed to alert)
 *   - alert fires ONLY if the burst is speech-shaped:
 *        peak >= alert level  AND  burst has lasted >= 250 ms
 *   - short spikes still get a BURST report but NO alert
 *
 * MEASURED 29 Sep (same speaker, same word):
 *   RL below collarbone: silence ~314, words 1556-1764 (5x)   <- stronger
 *   RL back of neck    : silence ~275, words 564-854  (2.3x)  <- current
 *
 * Board: ESP32 Dev Module, Baud 115200. Wiring same as always:
 *   AD8232: 3V3->3V3  GND->GND  OUT->GPIO34  LO+->GPIO32  LO-->GPIO33
 *
 * KEYS:  c calibrate (SILENT!)   +/- alert level x100   t test alert
 *        i info   r fast/slow   h/w/y/n/s marks
 */

const int PIN_OUT = 34, PIN_LOP = 32, PIN_LON = 33;
const int SAMPLE_MS = 2;
int printMs = 50;

long center = 2048;
int  env = 0, lastRaw = 0;
bool firstSample = true;
const int RING = 100;
int ring[RING]; int ringIdx = 0;

// ---------- detector V1.4 (shape gate + calibration) ----------
int  thresh   = 575;   // alert level: peak needed (default: RL back of neck)
int  burstLvl = 475;   // burst starts here  (default: RL back of neck)
const unsigned long BURST_GRACE_MS = 150;  // dips shorter than this stay in the burst
const unsigned long SPEECH_MIN_MS  = 250;  // burst must LAST this long to alert
const unsigned long REFRACTORY_MS  = 1500;

bool inBurst = false, firedThisBurst = false;
unsigned long burstStart = 0, lastHigh = 0, lastFire = 0;
int  burstPeak = 0, maxEnvEver = 0, helpCount = 0;

unsigned long tS = 0, tP = 0;

void printBanner() {
  Serial.println();
  Serial.println(F("==== VocalBridge HELP DETECTOR V1.4 (calibrated shape gate) ===="));
  Serial.println(F("baud=115200"));
  Serial.println(F("alert = peak >= alert level AND burst lasts >= 250 ms"));
  Serial.print(F("burst level=")); Serial.print(burstLvl);
  Serial.print(F("  alert level=")); Serial.print(thresh);
  Serial.println(F("  (defaults: RL on BACK OF NECK)"));
  Serial.println(F("green pad moved? press c while SILENT+STILL -> auto re-tune (5 s)"));
  Serial.println(F("measured: neck words 564-854 / collarbone words 1556-1764"));
  Serial.println(F("keys: c=calibrate, +/- alert, t=test, i=info, r=speed, marks h w y n s"));
  Serial.println(F("STATUE TEST: sit silent+still 20 s - alerts during it = wire/pad problem"));
  Serial.println(F("plotter: raw,env,peak,pads,thresh"));
  Serial.println(F("streaming..."));
}

void mark(const __FlashStringHelper *w) {
  Serial.print(F(">>>MARK:")); Serial.print(w);
  Serial.print(F(" t=")); Serial.print(millis()/1000.0, 2); Serial.println(F("s<<<"));
}

void fireHelp(unsigned long durMs) {
  helpCount++;
  Serial.println(F("############################################################"));
  Serial.print(F(">>>  HELP!  DETECTED  #")); Serial.print(helpCount);
  Serial.print(F("   peak=")); Serial.print(burstPeak);
  Serial.print(F("   dur=")); Serial.print(durMs);
  Serial.print(F("ms   max=")); Serial.print(maxEnvEver);
  Serial.print(F("   t=")); Serial.print(millis()/1000.0, 2); Serial.println(F("s"));
  Serial.println(F("############################################################"));
}

void reportBurst(unsigned long durMs) {
  Serial.print(F(">>> BURST peak=")); Serial.print(burstPeak);
  Serial.print(F(" dur=")); Serial.print(durMs);
  Serial.println(F("ms alert=no (too short or too weak - logged for study)"));
}

void runCalibrate() {
  Serial.println(F(">>> CALIBRATE: sit SILENT + STILL, do not talk... (5 s)"));
  const int N = 100;                     // 100 x 50 ms = 5 s
  int buf[N];
  for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
    unsigned long st = millis();
    while (millis() - st < 50) { sample(); delay(2); }
    buf[i] = env;
  }
  for (int i = 0; i < N - 1; i++)        // sort small array
    for (int j = i + 1; j < N; j++)
      if (buf[j] < buf[i]) { int tmp = buf[i]; buf[i] = buf[j]; buf[j] = tmp; }
  int med = (buf[N/2 - 1] + buf[N/2]) / 2;
  burstLvl = med + 200;
  thresh   = med + 300;
  inBurst = false; burstPeak = 0; firedThisBurst = false;
  Serial.print(F(">>> CALIBRATE done. silence=")); Serial.print(med);
  Serial.print(F("  burst="));  Serial.print(burstLvl);
  Serial.print(F("  alert="));  Serial.println(thresh);
  Serial.println(F(">>> if you talked during it, press c again"));
}

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);
  pinMode(PIN_LOP, INPUT); pinMode(PIN_LON, INPUT);
  analogReadResolution(12);
  analogSetPinAttenuation(PIN_OUT, ADC_11db);
  delay(800);
  printBanner();
}

void sample() {
  int raw = analogRead(PIN_OUT);
  lastRaw = raw;
  if (firstSample) { center = raw; firstSample = false; }
  center += (raw - center) / 1024;
  int dev = abs(raw - center);
  if (dev > env) env = dev;
  else           env = (env * 97) / 100;
  if (env > maxEnvEver) maxEnvEver = env;
  ring[ringIdx] = env;
  ringIdx = (ringIdx + 1) % RING;
}

void printLine() {
  int peak = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < RING; i++) if (ring[i] > peak) peak = ring[i];
  bool padsOn = (digitalRead(PIN_LOP) == LOW && digitalRead(PIN_LON) == LOW);
  Serial.print(F("raw:"));    Serial.print(lastRaw);
  Serial.print(F(",env:"));   Serial.print(env);
  Serial.print(F(",peak:"));  Serial.print(peak);
  Serial.print(F(",pads:"));  Serial.print(padsOn ? 1 : 0);
  Serial.print(F(",thresh:")); Serial.print(thresh);
  Serial.print(F("  [t="));   Serial.print(millis()/1000.0, 2); Serial.print(F("s]"));
  if (!padsOn) Serial.print(F("  CHECK-PADS!"));
  Serial.println();
}

void handleKey(char c) {
  if (c=='\r'||c=='\n'||c=='\t'||c==' ') return;
  if      (c=='h'||c=='H') mark(F("HELP"));
  else if (c=='w'||c=='W') mark(F("WATER"));
  else if (c=='y'||c=='Y') mark(F("YES"));
  else if (c=='n'||c=='N') mark(F("NO"));
  else if (c=='s'||c=='S') mark(F("SILENT-no-word"));
  else if (c=='t'||c=='T') {
    Serial.println(F("############################################################"));
    Serial.println(F(">>>  HELP!  (TEST - key t)"));
    Serial.println(F("############################################################"));
  }
  else if (c=='c'||c=='C') runCalibrate();
  else if (c=='+'||c=='=') { thresh += 100; Serial.print(F(">>> threshold=")); Serial.println(thresh); }
  else if (c=='-'||c=='_') { thresh -= 100; Serial.print(F(">>> threshold=")); Serial.println(thresh); }
  else if (c=='r'||c=='R') { printMs = (printMs==50)?250:50; Serial.println(printMs==250?F(">>>rate=slow"):F(">>>rate=fast")); }
  else if (c=='i'||c=='I') printBanner();
  else Serial.println(F("keys: c=calibrate, +/- thresh, t=test, i=info, r=speed, marks h w y n s"));
}

void loop() {
  unsigned long now = millis();
  if (now - tS >= (unsigned long)SAMPLE_MS) { tS = now; sample(); }

  // ---------- burst profiler + shape gate (V1.4) ----------
  if (env >= burstLvl) {
    if (!inBurst) { inBurst = true; burstStart = now; burstPeak = env; firedThisBurst = false; }
    if (env > burstPeak) burstPeak = env;
    lastHigh = now;
    unsigned long age = now - burstStart;
    if (!firedThisBurst && env >= thresh &&
        age >= SPEECH_MIN_MS && now - lastFire >= REFRACTORY_MS) {
      fireHelp(age);
      lastFire = now;
      firedThisBurst = true;
    }
  } else if (inBurst && now - lastHigh >= BURST_GRACE_MS) {
    reportBurst(now - burstStart);
    inBurst = false; burstPeak = 0;
  }

  if (now - tP >= (unsigned long)printMs) { tP = now; printLine(); }
  while (Serial.available()) handleKey(Serial.read());
}

void classifyBurst(unsigned long durMs) {
  // durMs = lastHigh - burstStart (time above burst level, grace excluded)
  if (burstPeak >= helpPeakMin && burstPeak <= HELP_PEAK_MAX &&
      durMs >= HELP_DUR_MIN && durMs <= HELP_DUR_MAX) {
    fireHelp(burstPeak, durMs);
  } else {
    Serial.print(F(">>> BURST peak=")); ... 
    reason: too weak / too strong / too short / too long
  }
}

registerBeat():
cpp


void registerBeat() {
  unsigned long now = millis();
  if (lastBeat && now - lastBeat > 5000 && pulseStorm) { end storm }
  // ring logic:
  beatTimes[beatIdx] = now; beatIdx = (beatIdx+1)%PULSE_N; if (beatCount < PULSE_N) beatCount++;
  lastBeat = now; beatsTotal++;
  if (beatCount == PULSE_N) {
    // check the 5 gaps using sorted order (ring order = chronological)
    bool regular = true;
    for (i in 1..PULSE_N-1) { gap = times[i]-times[i-1] (careful ring wrap: read in chronological order starting at beatIdx) }
    if (regular && !pulseStorm) { pulseStorm = true; bpm = 60000 / median gap (use avg gap); print warning ">>> PULSE DETECTED (~N bpm). The green pad is picking up your heartbeat - press it back on, then press c. No HELP alerts until it stops."; }
  }
  if (pulseStorm && beatsTotal % 20 == 0) { print ">>> PULSE still active (~N bpm) - fix green pad, then c"; }
}
